title: Applications and Evaluation of Foundation Models
objective: Compare models and generation methods that fit a use case based on quality, latency, cost, and safety.

sections.title: Choose a model based on the acceptance criteria for its intended use
paragraphs: Foundation models can be applied to a wide variety of tasks, but they do not offer the same quality, input formats, latency, pricing, or usage conditions. Using representative inputs, compare them against the same acceptance criteria for required quality, acceptable response time, expected usage volume, and safety.

sections.title: Separating Prompts, RAG, and Customization
paragraphs: First evaluate clear instructions and a small number of examples, then use Prompt Management to manage the versions and changes of approved prompts. Use RAG for up-to-date evidence and customization for specific behaviors that need to be maintained over time. Choose among methods such as continued pretraining, fine-tuning, and distillation by comparing the data, cost, evaluation, and operational responsibilities involved. For production agents, establish least-privilege tool permissions, approvals, and auditing.

sections.title: Evaluate Metrics and Business Outcomes Separately
paragraphs: For classification, use accuracy, precision—the correctness of results classified as positive—recall—the proportion of positives that should be found and were retrieved—and F1, which reflects the balance between them, according to the objective. For summarization and dialogue, combine automated metrics such as ROUGE with human evaluations of accuracy, evidence, and safety. Measure these model evaluations separately from business outcomes such as reduced processing time and fewer incorrect recommendations. Compare representative and failure-prone examples against the same acceptance criteria.

checkpoints.prompt: The head of an online retail company makes response quality and latency in the conversational interface acceptance criteria. What is the most appropriate way to compare the candidate models?

choices.text: Adopt the latest model without measuring it in practice.
choices.explanation: You cannot tell whether it meets the requirements.

choices.text: Compare quality and latency using representative conversational inputs and the same criteria.
choices.explanation: This lets you evaluate both factors in line with the use case.

choices.text: Choose the model that produces the longest responses.
choices.explanation: This is not an indicator of quality or latency.

checkpoints.prompt: A knowledge management specialist at a manufacturing company wants answers to reflect maintenance procedures revised every week. Which method avoids weekly retraining?

choices.text: Retrieve the latest version and add it to the context at generation time.
choices.explanation: RAG can ground the answer in the latest documents.

choices.text: Use only the model’s general knowledge.
choices.explanation: This cannot guarantee the latest company-specific procedures.

choices.text: Shorten the procedure manual and omit it from the input.
choices.explanation: This cannot incorporate the supporting information.

checkpoints.prompt: A quality manager at a financial institution wants to identify, before release, failures in which the summarization feature misinterprets important conditions. Which evaluation is most appropriate?

choices.text: Prepare representative documents and documents that are prone to failure, then verify condition preservation against common criteria.
choices.explanation: This addresses the intended use and the impact of failures.

choices.text: Measure only the number of output tokens.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for detecting fraudulent transactions wants to reduce the losses caused by missing actual fraud in particular. Which metric should they prioritize reviewing?

choices.explanation: This shows the proportion of actual fraud that was detected.
It shows how accurate the detected cases are, but it is insufficient for determining how much fraud was missed.
It does not represent detection performance.
It cannot be used to evaluate how often fraud is missed.
